name: Santorini
edition: Base game with god powers, Roxley rulesheet (2023 copyright, a living document)

source.title: Santorini base rulesheet (2023), Roxley file hosted on its store CDN, copy

setup.text: Fit the cliff pedestal onto the ocean board, then place the island board on top, matching the long and short tabs.
Pick one matchup from the Odyssey scorecard, or use the challenger method: the challenger draws 6 god cards and picks 2, chooses which god starts, and the opponent takes the other.
Take the god card for your side of the matchup. Both players should read each other's power before starting.
Take 2 workers of your colour. The player with the starting god places both on any empty spaces first, then the other player places theirs.

turn.summary: Pick one of your workers, move it, then build next to it. The player with the starting god goes first.
steps: Move the chosen worker to one of up to eight neighbouring spaces that is unoccupied (no worker and no dome).
You may move along the same level, down any number of levels, or up by one level at most.
Build a block or a dome on an unoccupied space next to the worker you moved. Use the correct piece for the level: a dome only goes on top of a third level.
Your god power may change these steps. Follow the card's wording.

end: The game ends the moment one player wins by climbing, or when a player cannot move and build and so loses.

scoring.text: There are no points. Win by moving a worker up onto a level 3 tower during your turn.
You also win if your opponent cannot complete a move and then a build on their turn.
Some god powers add their own win conditions.

missed.text: You must move and then build every turn. If you cannot do both, you lose at once.
You win only by moving up onto level 3. Being forced there by a power, or moving between two level 3 spaces, does not win.
Domes are not blocks. A power that affects blocks does not affect domes.
A forced worker has not moved. A power that says you cannot or must do something is binding, and breaking it loses the game.
A complete tower is three blocks and a dome. If you run out of a block type, remove a complete tower and put a dome on the ground in its place.

not_covered: 3 and 4 player games, which use mode cards that are not in the rulesheet text
Individual god powers, which are on the god cards
